Advanced Scientific Research' refers to the process in which a student, typically in their secondary level of education (grades 8-12), will identify a topic of their own choosing based on their own personal interests and curiosity and will develop an authentic research project to answer an original research question across fields spanning Natural Sciences, Technology & Engineering, Social Sciences, Business & Finance,... Working alongside expert mentors, students formulate their research question, design a methodology, collect and analyze data, and produce findings that are entirely their own. These findings are then written up as an academic paper and presented at local, national, and international science competitions and symposia with standout projects moving forward to publication in peer-reviewed journals.

At GSJ, we recognize that the most powerful driver behind every great research project is a student's genuine curiosity and passion for discovery and our scientific research program is built to channel exactly that into real, publishable, competition-ready work.

- Mentorship
Students are grouped into team (4-6 members) or potentially paired with professional scientists who act as their mentors throughout the program. The mentors provide guidance, knowledge, and support as the student undertakes research. 

- Research Report
Upon completion of their research, students are required to write an academic-level research paper detailing their methodology, results, and conclusions following standard scientific format and guidelines.

- Presentation
Students showcase their findings before a panel of experts at GSJ, various competitions, symposia, and science fairs at national and international levels. This provides them with the opportunity to communicate their research effectively and receive feedback from peers and professionals in the field.

- Publication
Exceptional research projects have the chance to be published in scientific journals, thereby contributing meaningfully to the scientific community. Moreover, students stand a chance to win accolades and recognition for their exemplary work through competitions and symposia.

- Fosters Curiosity & Creativity
Scientific research encourages students to explore their curiosity, think outside the box, and come up with innovative solutions to complex problems

- Hands-On Experience
Students gain practical experience in scientific research, learning essential skills in critical thinking, problem-solving, data analysis, and scientific writing.

- Professional Networking
By working closely with a mentor, students build valuable connections within the scientific community, opening doors to future opportunities in academia and industry. Students also learn to work collaboratively with peers and supervisors in a professional setting.

- Skill Development
The program hones students' skills in research design, experimentation, data interpretation, and presentation, laying a solid foundation for their future academic and professional pursuits.

- Enhances University Applications
Participation in scientific research demonstrates to university admissions officers a student's passion for learning, ability to work independently, and dedication to a particular field of study, giving applicants a competitive edge during the university admissions process.

1. Choose Topic
The first step is choosing a topic to study that you have a personal interest or curiosity about.

2. Develop Research Question
After reading some of the current published literature around your topic, you will develop a research question to investigate.

3. Create Research Plan
At this point, you will collaborate with your Research Coach and Mentor to create a research plan prior to starting your study.

4. Conduct Research
Students will conduct their research following the methodology they outlined in their research plan. This can be done in-person or remotely.

5. Conduct Analysis & Draw Conclusions
Students will analyze the data collected in their methodology to draw conclusions. These conclusions will be original findings in their field.

6. Present Findings
Write an academic paper and create visual presentations to share your findings with the world!

- GSJ staff are always available to address any questions or concerns that arise, providing responsive and attentive support to both mentors and students throughout the program.

- Guide students through the research process by sharing your knowledge, providing constructive feedback, and offering expertise in your field.

- Meet regularly with your mentee to review progress, discuss findings, and work through any challenges that arise.

- Review and provide feedback on data analysis, paper drafts, and presentations as the project approaches completion.

- Maintain open communication with GSJ staff to support student progress and uphold academic integrity throughout the program.

- Research engagements can be conducted remotely or in-person, depending on the nature of each research project.

- Mentors are expected to commit to a 5 to 6 month engagement, with one session of approximately 2.5 to 3 hours per week per project.
